children: Nearly two years after the Federal Reserve delivered the first rate cut of the last easing cycle, Citi economists now expect U.S. policymakers to raise the federal funds rate this week.
Additionally, they do not anticipate a prolonged tightening campaign. Any increase, they argue, is more likely to be described as a calibration than as the opening move of a new hiking cycle.

The change in tone is not limited to Washington. For the first time in years, more major central banks are raising rates than cutting them. The European Central Bank has already begun tightening; Citi recently added two further hikes to its ECB forecast. The firm has also revised its Bank of England outlook and now looks for two additional increases. The Bank of Japan, meanwhile, is projected to deliver four rate rises in total.

Together these adjustments mark a notable turn in the global policy narrative. After an extended period in which easing dominated, officials in several large economies are again emphasizing the need to keep inflation from reaccelerating, even as they stop short of signaling an aggressive, multi-year tightening path.

title: Citi: Fed to hike this week — calls it a ‘calibration,’ not a new cycle
